text:
maya: Quick heads up — I'm planning a Terraform change to split per-model feature flags out of the global `redwood-config` ConfigMap and into per-model ConfigMaps that are sourced from ExternalSecrets. Want a quick rollout/readiness check before I open the PR.

infra-bot: Automated plan preview for change by maya

infra-bot: terraform plan will replace 3 resources and create 9.

maya: Rough plan: create `configmap/model-<model>` for each model, add `kubernetes_external_secret` resources that sync from SSM, and change `deployment` podTemplate to mount the per-model config via projected volumes. Aim is zero-downtime for most routes, but some pods may need rolling restarts when a new model config appears.

kevin: Will TF actually recreate the global configmap or just create new ones? If it replaces the old global config map we could accidentally trigger mass restarts.

maya: TF plan shows `-/+` on the global configmap (replaced) because we're moving keys out. It also shows new `kubernetes_config_map.model-foo` resources. Example snippet:
```
-/+ kubernetes_config_map.redwood_config
  ~ data.foo = "old" -> (sensitive)
  + data (9 new keys)
```

sarah: If the global configmap gets replaced that will trigger a rollout for every deployment that mounts it. We should avoid that. Two options: 1) keep the global CM around as a compatibility shim that reads from per-model CMS (less desired), or 2) change the deployments to reference per-model projected volumes and roll them incrementally.

alejandro: We should also consider using the `checksum/config-<model>` annotation pattern on Deployments. That lets us control which deployments restart and when.

maya: I'm planning to add a `checksum/config-<model>` annotation that we update only when the per-model secret changes, and wire the deployment rollout strategy to `maxUnavailable: 1` for safer rollouts. Also will add a short lived canary stack in `staging` to validate config loading.

kevin: sgtm. One more: ExternalSecrets sync timing — if we switch immediately, pods might mount empty files until sync completes. Can we pre-seed the ExternalSecrets -> k8s secret before switching the mount?

maya: Yes. Terraform will create the ExternalSecret + trigger the external-secrets-controller to populate the k8s Secret. I'll add a small `local-exec` null_resource that waits for `kubectl get secret model-foo --namespace infra` with a timeout before continuing to update the deployment manifest (so TF plan->apply won't leave pods with missing files).

sarah: Prefer avoiding local-exec if possible. Can we instead have the deployment tolerate missing mounts for a short startup window and have the app retry reads on 5xx? That keeps the infra apply pure.

maya: Good point. We can add `initContainer` that waits until the secret file exists. I'll prototype that in the staging overlay.

alejandro: PR link when ready? I'll review the TF logic for state move/import.

maya: Opening PR in a few mins: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412 :eyes:

kevin: pinged on PR, leaving comments about not replacing `redwood-config` in-place. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-checklist created #infra-deploy-queue/412

maya: Thanks all — will land to staging tonight after a short canary. If anything looks off I'll roll back the ExternalSecret and revert the TF apply. If you see anything in the PR tag me.

kevin: Sounds good. If you need help with the checksum helper script I can add it as a small Makefile target.

maya: Perfect. Assigning kevin and alejandro as reviewers. :rocket:
